description: Writing through an indexed mutable reference requires mutable access to the vector.
Compound assignment through an indexed mutable reference requires mutable vector access.
Explicitly borrowing an indexed referent mutably requires mutable vector access.
An annotated mutable-reference initializer requires mutable vector access even before a write.
Passing an indexed reference to an &mut parameter requires mutable vector access.
An &mut self call through a reference stored in a vector requires mutable vector access.
A mutable reference in a struct field does not bypass the vector indexing requirement.
Dereferencing a Box and its stored mutable reference after vector indexing still requires a mutable vector.
Array indexing after vector indexing cannot bypass the vector's mutable-access requirement.
A mutable reference to an inner vector does not provide mutable access to the outer vector.
An immutable Box<Vec<&mut T>> cannot supply mutable access to the vector.
A shared reference to a vector prevents mutation through its stored mutable references.
The valid immutable owned-array case does not permit mutation through a shared array reference.
The valid immutable owned-Box case does not permit mutation through a shared Box reference.
Mutable vectors permit assignment, compound assignment, explicit borrowing, annotated mutable-reference initializers, and &mut arguments.
An immutable binding holding &mut Vec permits indexed writes, mutable arguments, and &mut method receivers.
Shared coercions, explicit shared borrows, and shared method receivers need no mutable vector access.
Immutable owned arrays, structs, and Boxes permit mutation through their stored mutable references.
A mutable reference reached through an immutable array or Box can supply access before indexing a vector.
Mutable vectors permit writes through nested struct fields, Boxes, arrays, and mutable vector references.
Moving a vector to a mutable binding or temporary gives indexing the new place's mutability.
Mutating a separate copy or explicit clone does not require mutable access to the original vector.
